title: Assessment of Intracavernosal Pressure in a Rat Model
author: Shankun Zhao
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.kwdcxa6
materials: The ES equipment was composed of a bipolar hook electrode and an integrated data acquisition system (MP 150A-CE; Biopac, Santa Barbara, CA). All data were analyzed using the AcqKnowledge software, version 4.2.1 (Biopac System Inc). The application of different voltages and frequencies were used in the current protocol to achieve a significant and consistent erectile response. Under anaesthetic (pentobarbital, 45 mg/kg), rats were firstly subjected to sequential stimulation strengths ranging from 1 to 10 volts at a frequency of 15 Hz with a square pulse wave form and a duration of 5 milliseconds for 60 seconds. The optimal voltage parameter according to the voltage response curves was logged. Next, the effect of different frequencies (10, 15 and 20 Hz) at the selected voltage that resulted in the highest erectile response was assessed. Three ESs were replicated at intervals of 5 min.

Basal ICP was firstly assessed using the analysis software of AcqKnowledge 4.2.1. The neurostimulation of the CN was next performed and the changes of ICP were recorded. The mean maximum ICP and the total ICP of the tumescence determined by the AUC from the beginning to the end of the CN stimulation (60 seconds) were recorded. The ES was always done in triplets with a 5-minute interval between the subsequent stimulations to ensure stable activity in every rat.

steps.title: Cannulate Right Carotid Artery
steps.instruction: Expose the right carotid artery, ligate its cephalad end with a 4‑0 silk suture, tie a slipknot with silk around the proximal end, insert a 24‑G angiocatheter pre‑filled with heparin and connected to a pressure transducer caudally into the artery, then tighten the slipknot to secure the sensor needle.

substeps.instruction: Ligate the cephalad end using a 4‑0 silk suture.
Tie a slipknot with silk around the proximal end of the artery.
Insert a 24‑G angiocatheter filled with heparin and connected to a pressure transducer caudally into the carotid artery.
Tighten the slipknot to prevent the sensor needle from falling out.

steps.title: Expose Prostate and Isolate Cavernous Nerve
steps.instruction: Retract the intestine, seminal vesicles, and bladder laterally with cotton swabs to expose the posterior fascial layer over the prostate; locate the atrophic prostate and the star‑like MPG posterolaterally adjacent to the dorsal prostate lobe and internal iliac vein; isolate the cavernous nerve (CN) using a glass needle; place a 0.3‑mm stainless steel bipolar hook electrode around the CN 2–4 mm distal to the MPG, positioning the positive electrode proximal to the MPG and the negative electrode distal, separate the electrode hooks with a 1‑mm diameter insulator, and encase the stimulator ends in a piece of latex glove to avoid stimulation of surrounding tissue.

substeps.instruction: Retract intestine, seminal vesicles, and bladder laterally using cotton swabs.
Expose the fascial layer covering the posterior prostate.
Visualize the star‑like MPG posterolaterally, using the internal iliac vein as a landmark.
Isolate the cavernous nerve (CN) with a glass needle.
Place a tiny stainless steel bipolar hook electrode (0.3 mm diameter) around the CN 2–4 mm distal to the MPG.
Position the positive electrode proximal to the MPG and the negative electrode at the distal end.
Separate the parallel hooks with a 1‑mm diameter insulator.
Encapsulate the stimulator ends in a piece of latex glove to prevent electrical stimulation of surrounding tissues.

steps.title: Insert ICP Needle and Prime with Heparin
steps.instruction: Deglove the penis, bluntly dissect the penile ischiocavernous muscle to one side to expose the tunica albuginea of the crus of the corpus cavernosum, insert a 24‑gauge venoclysis needle into the side of the crus (or midpoint of the corpus cavernosum) for ICP measurement, and inject 50 µL of heparinized saline (250 U/mL) through a T‑shaped connection pipe to prevent clotting of the needle tip.

substeps.instruction: Bluntly dissect the penile ischiocavernous muscle to one side to expose the tunica albuginea of the crus of the corpus cavernosum.
Insert a 24‑gauge venoclysis needle into the side of the crus (or midpoint of the corpus cavernosum) for ICP measurement.
Inject 50 µL of heparinized saline (250 U/mL) via a syringe through the T‑shaped connection pipe to prevent clotting of the needle tip.
